content_preview.title: Optimizely Supply-Chain Breach Injected Crypto-Clipper and Card-Skimmer Malware Into 178 Organizations' Sites, Including CNN and BBC
content_preview.summary: Attackers exploited an Optimizely Experimentation signup flaw to inject malware into 188 of 1,611 scanned customer JavaScript snippets, Optimizely confirmed.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Optimizely, a web experimentation and personalization platform whose JavaScript snippets are embedded directly into customer websites, confirmed on November 16, 2026, that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to inject malicious code into customer projects, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/optimizely-supply-chain-attack-delivers-malware-to-cnn-fox-news-bbc-salesforce-sites/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know), 691 words within the 400-1200 News range. Neutral, factual tone throughout, no sensationalism or editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 6 source snapshots in full from sources/2026-11/optimizely-supply-chain-breach-injected-crypto-clipper-and-card-skimmer-malware-into-178-organizations-sites-including-cnn-and-bbc/ after gunzip and sha256 verification (all six hashes matched manifest.json exactly: source-0 through source-5). source-0 (BleepingComputer, archive_fallback via Wayback Machine, original returned 200) independently confirmed via urlscan.io that the malicious script loaded on BBC and CNN pages among others. source-1 (Help Net Security) quotes Helme verbatim: 'The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock' -- confirms 178 orgs, 188/1,611 snippet count, banks=32 largest group, and the Optimizely statement quoted verbatim in the article. source-2 (The Register) confirms the OPTIMJACK name, the 1,611/188 figures, the Optimizely statement verbatim, and TalkTalk as the last infected org at 21:52 UTC. source-3 (StepSecurity) is the most detailed technical writeup: confirms CNN/BBC/Fox News had the payload file itself captured by urlscan, the 8-cryptocurrency clipper with checksum-validated swapping, the Luhn-check card skimmer, Coruna (iOS 13-17) and DarkSword (iOS 18.x) exploit kits, the $7,040 figure as of 19:25 UTC Nov 16, the 04:21 UTC first BBC injection and 13:43 UTC card-skimmer addition, and the unresolved question of how the signup-flow bug granted cross-project write access. source-4 (Malwarebytes) independently confirms CNN/BBC/Zoom naming, the ~190,000-site Optimizely install base, and gives the full BBC timeline verbatim: clean capture 02:21 UTC -> injected 04:21 UTC -> main payload observed live on bbc.com by 08:28 UTC -> Report URI's monitored files clean by 23:11 UTC. source-5 (heise.de, in English translation) independently confirms CNN/BBC/HSBC/IKEA/Equifax naming and the $7,040 figure (reported as ~EUR6,400 at 8:25pm CET = 19:25 UTC), matching StepSecurity's figure and timestamp exactly. All direct quotes in the article (Optimizely's statement, Helme's 'multi-purpose kit' quote) are verbatim matches to the snapshots. No hallucinated quotes or fabricated specifics found. Minor note: the sentence bundling the BBC timeline and the 20:40-23:11 cleanup window cites 'StepSecurity and Malwarebytes' jointly for a compound claim where each outlet actually supplies a different piece of the range (StepSecurity: 04:21 injection, 13:43 skimmer, 20:40 cleanup start; Malwarebytes: 02:21 clean baseline, 08:28 BBC-specific payload-live confirmation, 23:11 cleanup end) -- the two sources are fully consistent with each other and every individual timestamp is independently verified in at least one snapshot, so this is a citation-bundling style choice rather than a misattribution or fabrication, and does not warrant a corrections record.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Ran the policy's claim-accuracy quantifier scan (absence/quantifier/superlative terms) against the submission body. Checked 'last organization' (TalkTalk, confirmed by The Register), 'largest single victim group' (banks, 32, confirmed by Help Net Security and StepSecurity), '1,611/188/178... both outlets reported' (confirmed independently by Help Net Security and The Register, the two outlets cited in the preceding sentence), and 'None of the cited sources reported a final, confirmed count of recovered funds or whether law enforcement had opened an investigation' (verified true across all 6 snapshots -- none mentions a final recovery tally or a law-enforcement probe). All derived/vendor figures ($7,040, 1,611/188, 178 orgs, 32 banks, 8 cryptocurrencies, iOS version ranges) were recomputed/cross-checked against raw source text, not taken from the writer's own summary.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Attack mechanics and victim list are reported factually with attribution; no loaded language.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Optimizely or this campaign found (grep across src/content/articles/ for 'optimizely' returned no hits). Genuinely new topic.
editor_notes.headline_verification: Special scrutiny applied per editorial instruction to the headline's naming of CNN and BBC as breach victims. This is NOT a hedge or an overstated 'may have included' claim -- it rests on firm, independently corroborated technical evidence: BleepingComputer independently confirmed via urlscan.io scan data that the malicious script loaded on BBC and CNN pages; StepSecurity reports urlscan captured the exact payload file itself (SHA-256 f7b84b9a...) served with HTTP 200 on CNN and BBC pages between 17:57-21:23 UTC; Help Net Security quotes Helme's own list naming BBC and CNN; The Register, Malwarebytes, and heise.de each independently list BBC and CNN among the confirmed-affected organizations. Five of six sources corroborate this specific claim with technical evidence, not speculation. The headline claim is solid.
editor_notes.anthropic_disclosure: Anthropic disclosure: not required - the story concerns a third-party web-experimentation vendor's supply-chain breach and is unrelated to Anthropic, Claude, or any Anthropic-operated product.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced News piece on a major supply-chain security incident. All 6 sources read in full and cross-verified; every specific figure, quote, and timestamp traces to at least one cited snapshot, with most of the headline-critical facts (CNN/BBC naming, victim counts, dollar figures) independently corroborated by multiple outlets. No fabrications, no misattributions, no orphan sources, no suspicious patterns in any snapshot. Featured candidacy: 2 - a major, technically substantiated supply-chain breach hitting 178 organizations including globally recognized brands (CNN, BBC, HSBC, IKEA, Salesforce), with real consumer-facing impact (crypto theft, card skimming, iOS exploit delivery) that merits broad-audience visibility.
